model_interpretation.claim: For large n, a default-stream memset followed by one CTA-local reduction and one atomicAdd per CTA may avoid the baseline's multiple reduction launches and final copy. Larger CTA tiles reduce the number of contending atomics but increase per-CTA input work. The non-atomic control shares the tiled first-pass kernel structure; performance remains unmeasured and may regress due to memset or atomic contention.

items.subject: Single-kernel atomic finalization with explicit output initialization
items.objective: Test a one-kernel large-n path: zero out with cudaMemsetAsync on the default stream, then have each CTA reduce its input tile locally and contribute exactly one sum with atomicAdd. Sweep CTA tile size to expose the tradeoff between input work and atomic contention, but avoid per-element atomics and global partial-buffer reduction in this path. Compare the full memset-plus-kernel path with a non-atomic two-kernel control using the same first-pass tile and block mapping, so initialization and finalization costs are visible. Use current input data, no extra allocations, and no stale scratch dependencies; preserve correctness and tail safety for every valid input. Report repeated whole-call timings even if this approach loses.
